scope: Existing maintained filesystem engines operating on disposable regular-file images
Cold QEMU execution of the existing independent Nieuw OS kernel
Read-only foreign filesystem data images with before/after SHA256
Observed backend admission, data readability, corruption detection and recovery
Source-bound portability, licence and resource limitations
non_goals: No independent filesystem driver or new disk format
No replacement of the Nieuw OS kernel
No physical devices, raw host disks, production data or production keys
No global package installation, kernel modules or loop mounts
No claim of physical power-loss safety or product acceptance from host tests

owners.root: Integration, review-source documentation and progress assessment, final gate report
owners.project_architecture: native/ runner, isolated build and read-only native probes
owners.linux_filesystems: btrfs/ extracted tools, disposable images, corruption and salvage checks
owners.platforms: openzfs/ extracted tools, file-vdev engine and fresh-process recovery checks

acceptance.native_adoption: Existing engine executes through the independent kernel and reads/verifies the known corpus; missing implementation remains NOT_ACCEPTED
acceptance.host_recovery: Fresh process recovers known durable content with independent SHA256/metadata comparison; tool exit alone is insufficient
acceptance.mutation_boundary: Foreign native images attached read-only and full-image SHA256 unchanged
acceptance.evidence: Exact argv, tool/package versions, exit codes, stdout/stderr, mutation details, source and artifact hashes
acceptance.failure_reporting: Expected negative test success is distinct from filesystem adoption; blocked or unrun cases remain explicit

runtime_exception: OpenZFS ztest may create its standard /tmp/ztest.data.XXXXXX mkstemp and immediately unlink it; pools remain in its assigned disposable directory.
confirmation_scope: Four additional native runs after new upstream integration; original evidence retained unchanged.
